<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-blip2-9ce69b95" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fff6daeb7b674ec">Are Q-Former queries the text of the question to answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are a fixed number of learnable vectors, not the user&#x27;s question. Cross-attention reads tokens from the frozen vision encoder and passes selected information to the language side. Their fixed count forms a visual bottleneck: more complex images do not automatically produce more output tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four learnable queries can attend to hundreds of image patches while sending only four vectors to the language model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fff6daeb7b674ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-49e7f356a5e01708">How can Q-Former learn to connect images to a language model when both the vision encoder and language model are frozen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gradients can still flow through frozen modules to the connector; only parameter updates are frozen. Learnable queries select visual information through cross-attention and are projected into soft prompts the language model can consume. Two training stages address vision–language representation alignment and the generation interface. The bottleneck can still lose detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compressing 16 image features into four queries gives the language model four visual prompts, but reading small text may need more capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49e7f356a5e01708">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-56462053ed6b555f">How does BLIP-2&#x27;s interface differ from linearly projecting each visual patch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-patch projection primarily changes feature dimensions and usually preserves token count. Q-Former actively aggregates visual information with learnable queries before projection. This changes both selection and sequence length; lost detail depends on training and the task, not architecture alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clothing recognition may need only an outline, while reading small text may need local detail. Four queries are not guaranteed to suffice for both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56462053ed6b555f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-519bd14a28b1f0be">Do the local four-query results validate the paper&#x27;s two-stage pretraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local work uses real Fashion-MNIST pixels and four-query cross-attention, without ViT-g, a large LM, ITC/ITM/ITG, or large-scale second-stage training. It checks token compression and small-budget behavior, not original zero-shot capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reducing 16 visual tokens to four proves this interface shortens the sequence, not that it pretrained on over 100 million images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-519bd14a28b1f0be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:clip" data-paper-title="Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-clip-b03c09f0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a637592f066a62d1">Why can CLIP do zero-shot classification without retraining a classifier head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aclip">Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate encoders normalize image and class-description vectors and compare them in a shared space. The descriptions are class prototypes and can be replaced to define new labels. This depends on pretraining and does not guarantee arbitrary new concepts or fine-grained relationships are recognized.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare a shoe image with descriptions such as “a shoe” and “a coat,” then choose the higher similarity without training another linear head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a637592f066a62d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:clip" data-paper-title="Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48eaa29686fc2e90">Why does CLIP use both image-to-text and text-to-image contrastive learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aclip">Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same batch supplies two classification problems: find each image&#x27;s paired text and each text&#x27;s paired image. Both directions shape the shared similarity space. Other in-batch pairs provide negatives, but overall matching scores do not establish fine-grained factual accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cat and dog images pair with their respective descriptions, and both retrieval directions should rank each matching pair first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48eaa29686fc2e90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:clip" data-paper-title="Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d51dbad1f172823e">How do CLIP&#x27;s class text embeddings differ from autoregressive label generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aclip">Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CLIP compares similarities among supplied class texts and returns a choice or ranking within the candidates. An autoregressive model predicts a label token sequence that requires generation and parsing. CLIP&#x27;s descriptions are input prototypes, not generated targets, so this interface does not provide open-ended captioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Given “a photo of a cat” and “a photo of a dog,” CLIP compares their scores without generating “This is a cat.”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d51dbad1f172823e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:clip" data-paper-title="Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54de2a460ec3a509">Why normalize each vector before computing CLIP&#x27;s similarity matrix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aclip">Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalization makes dot products track direction instead of letting vector norms inflate scores; temperature controls sharpness. Matching pairs are on the diagonal, and the two directional losses use the matrix and its transpose. Not every pairing is a positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling an image vector should not make it more correct for every text. With unit normalization only a direction change alters cosine similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54de2a460ec3a509">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cue2narrate-drl" data-paper-title="From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-cue2narrate-drl-b44764fd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c735438cc2e66022">Why pair the negative caption with the same visual cue and prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acue2narrate-drl">From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TU Darmstadt &amp; hessian.AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching conditions isolates whether the descriptions suit the intended audio-description task. Changing image or prompt could instead change task difficulty. Offline negative captions are training material, not an extra deployment generation step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score “She sets down the cup” and an unrelated-action caption with the same film clip and instruction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01725v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.01725-cue2narrate-drl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c735438cc2e66022">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cue2narrate-drl" data-paper-title="From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-611aae51c5d5db99">Why backpropagate through a negative caption&#x27;s current likelihood if a frozen model generated it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acue2narrate-drl">From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TU Darmstadt &amp; hessian.AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing its generator fixes the negative text, not the trainable model&#x27;s scores. DRL compares mean target-token log likelihoods for positive and negative texts with the same visual input. Gradients improve their relative preference; detaching the negative score changes the contrastive optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For the same scene, one caption says a person walks and the other says they run. The strings are fixed, but the trainable model still changes their relative scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01725v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.01725-cue2narrate-drl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-611aae51c5d5db99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cue2narrate-drl" data-paper-title="From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bcd2ec1cbd06a88">What does DRL add beyond SFT on positive descriptions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acue2narrate-drl">From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TU Darmstadt &amp; hessian.AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT raises correct target-token likelihood; DRL explicitly separates positive and negative mean log probabilities. This adds a relative signal whose meaning depends on how negatives are built. Trivial negatives do not automatically teach detailed visual grounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raising the likelihood of “She sits down” need not lower the model&#x27;s score for the wrong “She runs away.” The relative loss constrains the pair directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01725v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.01725-cue2narrate-drl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bcd2ec1cbd06a88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cue2narrate-drl" data-paper-title="From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8bcd9e2f80d297e">Can SFT and DRL use one shared length normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acue2narrate-drl">From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TU Darmstadt &amp; hessian.AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The pinned SFT sums valid target tokens per sample before the batch mean. DRL averages token log probabilities separately in each description. Both exclude prompt and padding; freezing the negative generator does not stop gradients through the current model&#x27;s negative-caption scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For 10 positive tokens and 20 negative tokens, DRL compares their means. Raw sums would additionally penalize the longer description.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01725v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.01725-cue2narrate-drl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8bcd9e2f80d297e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-cv-opd-6105b27e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fbea63986417aa5">Why prepare positive and negative crops from the same image in CV-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The positive provides local evidence; the same-image, same-size, low-overlap negative is a visual counterfactual. The student sees the full image, while teacher inputs differ only in region. This tests whether learning follows the evidence rather than a language prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a street sign, use the sign in the positive crop and nearby wall in the negative crop. Both teachers share parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fbea63986417aa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be9768a40b798c69">Why does CV-OPD give both teachers the same student prefix and change only the visual crop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Differences then primarily come from the region, not text history. On its own rollout prefixes, the student moves toward the correct-region teacher and away from the negative-region teacher by a bounded JSD margin. This addresses answer distillation that might learn only a language prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For cup color, the positive crop shows the cup and the same-size negative crop shows background. Both teachers see identical student-generated text so far.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be9768a40b798c69">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ad827d370c8181c">What does CDL add over distillation from a positive-crop teacher alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive-only distillation pulls the student toward the positive distribution. CDL also requires sufficient JSD from the negative teacher using a margin on a bounded divergence. It neither requires unlimited separation nor guarantees improvements on every benchmark.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student equally close to both teachers may have low positive-only loss, but still incur a margin penalty for failing to distinguish regions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ad827d370c8181c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-438df272d6627df3">If at least one rollout is correct, should the other rollouts be dropped?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep all rollouts of a sample that passes the at-least-one-correct gate. DAG gates tokens across the retained batch with JSD strictly above the mean. Teachers, generation, and gate do not backpropagate. The top-100 JSD approximation must preserve the full tail bucket.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one of eight rollouts is correct, keep all eight; removing the other seven changes the training distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 本地结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-438df272d6627df3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:embedding-gemma2" data-paper-title="EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-embedding-gemma2-1f83fce4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d009645d6382686">Does a shared 768-dimensional space require all four modalities at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aembedding-gemma2">EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A shared space lets all modalities use comparable vector similarities, while towers load as needed. Supported inputs and actually verified paths differ. Local official-checkpoint validation covers text and images only, not audio and video pipelines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Image-to-text search needs only the image and text paths; their validation does not establish audio retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d009645d6382686">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:embedding-gemma2" data-paper-title="EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1671088f314bae5">Why renormalize a truncated Matryoshka embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aembedding-gemma2">EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The retained prefix generally no longer has unit norm. Raw dot products would mix differences in retained energy with similarity. Renormalizing restores cosine scale. This relies on trained prefix representations, not arbitrary truncation, and pooling must exclude padding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Truncate two 768-dimensional vectors to 128 dimensions and normalize each again so larger retained norms do not confer an advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1671088f314bae5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:embedding-gemma2" data-paper-title="EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eed6fdf443ec6128">How does MRL truncation differ from randomly dropping dimensions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aembedding-gemma2">EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MRL trains designated prefixes, such as 128, 256, or 512 dimensions, to serve as representations after renormalization. Random subsets lack that training convention. Shorter prefixes save storage and retrieval cost, but quality must be reported by task and fixed size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Taking the first 128 of 768 dimensions follows the trained contract; randomly drawing 128 each time is a different compression method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eed6fdf443ec6128">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:embedding-gemma2" data-paper-title="EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a5d62a51c0cdd94">The formal paper pools before projection, but the local path pools official last_hidden_state. Is a layer missing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aembedding-gemma2">EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The pinned official implementation applies a bias-free embedding_projection before returning its 768-dimensional token states. Equal-weight masked mean commutes with linear projection, so pooling those outputs matches the paper; projecting again would be incorrect. The formal paper does not upgrade the existing 16-image GPU run to seven full benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Averaging two tokens after multiplying each by the same matrix equals averaging first and then multiplying. Nonlinearity or token-dependent transformations break this equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a5d62a51c0cdd94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:embedding-gemma2" data-paper-title="EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1730598e354b01ed">What details matter for mean pooling, truncation, and precision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aembedding-gemma2">EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention-mask pooling excludes padding, followed by prefix truncation and L2 renormalization. Queries and documents use their respective text prefixes; images use none. Official activation ranges can produce non-finite FP16 values, so the local path pins FP32 and rejects non-finite or zero vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical text padded to different lengths should yield the same masked representation. Including padding makes it length-dependent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1730598e354b01ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-flexglue-0459516f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e891739cff8d495">How does FlexGlue&#x27;s dense grid support arbitrary-position queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Features interact globally on a stride-8 grid. Interpolation reads the requested coordinate&#x27;s feature, and cross-image attention estimates the corresponding location. Queries need not coincide with cell centers or be restricted to fixed keypoints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a query between four cells, interpolate its feature before matching instead of snapping to the nearest cell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e891739cff8d495">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8472fbb022dc303">Why does FlexGlue read coordinates near a peak rather than take a global expectation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar structures can create several peaks, making a global average land between valid matches. A local window around the strongest candidate avoids averaging modes; refinement then predicts a displacement. Covisibility votes and hard negatives separately assess whether the images are matchable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two identical windows score highly, the global average lands on the wall. Read coordinates around the chosen window for a plausible starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8472fbb022dc303">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-55aa95e8e4472093">When does FlexGlue&#x27;s layer-wise covisibility gate exit early?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every layer produces token-level sigmoid votes. Exit when the mean across both images falls below that layer&#x27;s threshold tγ^(L−k). This tests whether matching should continue, not just the strongest local match. Reliability of the gate matters; fewer layers do not prove higher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two symmetric buildings can contain nearly identical local features but have low overall covisibility, so exit rather than refine a confident false match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55aa95e8e4472093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4c29d72335d48b2">Can ordinary softmax and cross-entropy reproduce FlexGlue&#x27;s coarse matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The paper uses 1.5-entmax and Fenchel–Young loss, with bilinear weights on four cells surrounding the subpixel target and detached coarse coordinates during refinement. No full local operator, training metrics, or GPU receipt exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A target at a four-cell junction gives all four weights. Snapping to one cell changes the supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4c29d72335d48b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:gslm2" data-paper-title="GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-gslm2-6098f74c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91f98a46762c2366">Why not deduplicate each GSLM2 speech stream independently and then concatenate the columns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Agslm2">GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different streams can change on different audio frames. After independent deduplication, entry k can refer to different times. GSLM2 retains the union of change frames and reads all streams at each retained time, preserving real alignment for the shared temporal backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A = [1,1,2] and B = [4,5,5] retain (1,4), (1,5), (2,5). Independent deduplication and zipping would place (2,5) second and lose the actual middle tuple (1,5).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91f98a46762c2366">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:gslm2" data-paper-title="GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7659a67c5a28786">Why does paired transition scoring average within streams before averaging across streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Agslm2">GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Streams change at different rates. Normalizing by each stream&#x27;s count, including its first unit, and then weighting streams equally prevents a fast-changing stream from dominating by event count. Persistent units remain in the conditioning input but not in their stream&#x27;s transition average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Valid log probabilities are [−4] and [−1,−2,−3,−4]. The stream means −4 and −2.5 give −3.25. Pooling five events gives −2.8 instead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7659a67c5a28786">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:gslm2" data-paper-title="GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-542025fa89124915">Why isn&#x27;t the stream-specific transition score a joint likelihood from the multi-stream generation head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Agslm2">GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transition head sees previous multi-stream tuples and scores only the first unit and changes in its own stream. The generation head conditions sequentially within a time step and predicts every retained position, including a stream&#x27;s repeats. Both conditioning and scored events differ, and paired accuracy is not continuation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The second stream in a generated tuple can read the first stream&#x27;s newly generated unit at that step. A stream-specific scoring head for the second stream sees previous time steps, not the first stream at the current step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-542025fa89124915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:gslm2" data-paper-title="GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96450e58e318a5ef">How do you test that retaining repeated units as context does not accidentally score them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Agslm2">GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Supply aligned retained tuples and externally computed target log probabilities. With tuples fixed, perturb scores only at unchanged positions in one stream; its mean and the final score must stay fixed. Changing its first or transition score must affect the result. Independently check the retained raw frame indices; this unit test is not a speech benchmark.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep the second tuple in (2,5) → (2,6). Changing its first-stream score from −100 to −1 cannot change the aggregate, whereas changing its second-stream score should.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96450e58e318a5ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gas" data-paper-title="Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gas-1fb6a8b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a203eea136c296da">Does GAS next-embedding prediction output discrete image tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agas">Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It predicts continuous embeddings in the LM&#x27;s visual input space, with cosine alignment to an EMA-projected target. It does not classify a discrete image codebook. Generation is auxiliary to understanding and deployment need not generate images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the direction of a target patch embedding instead of choosing an index from thousands of image codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12209">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12209-gas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a203eea136c296da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gas" data-paper-title="Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f6e57e97260ca61">Why can GAS remove its entire auxiliary generation branch at deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agas">Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>During training it predicts continuous visual embeddings and backpropagates into a lower vision path shared with understanding. Its upper generation parameters are separate and not used by inference. Removing the branch retains the trained shared parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train on image understanding and target visual embeddings, then deploy only image question answering with the learned shared vision path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12209">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12209-gas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f6e57e97260ca61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gas" data-paper-title="Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea7ba395bdabb73a">How does GAS next-embedding prediction differ from reconstructing the current patch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agas">Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>NEP predicts the next position from prior visual embeddings and allowed autoregressive context; an EMA projection supplies the target. Feeding the target at the same position changes what the model sees and can reduce the task to copying. Removability of the branch does not replace the shifted objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To predict visual embedding i, provide earlier positions and allowed context, not embedding i itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12209">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12209-gas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea7ba395bdabb73a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gas" data-paper-title="Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1371d6b9ed359eda">Why check inference dependencies before claiming GAS adds no deployment parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agas">Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generation upper layers, vision head, and EMA projector are removable only if understanding no longer reads them. Training still needs shifted prediction, EMA targets, and branch isolation. A local mirror-target diagnostic cannot validate the gains of large-scale generative data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Feeding an intermediate generation output back into understanding keeps that branch necessary at inference despite a claim of zero added parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12209">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12209-gas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1371d6b9ed359eda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lamp" data-paper-title="LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-lamp-52f612c4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f533d9685d57ba72">Relative to what does LAMP compute its label residuals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alamp">LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taizhou Institute of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtract the original CLIP text-prototype scores from true support labels. Each layer&#x27;s kernel predictor corrects the prior rather than relearning all classes. If prototypes change, the residual must follow or the correction no longer matches its target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a cat support image has a low CLIP cat score, the kernel branch learns the difference rather than retraining the vision encoder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22182-lamp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f533d9685d57ba72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lamp" data-paper-title="LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d272f3c9d6e7debd">Why mix LAMP&#x27;s layer predictions in class-score space rather than concatenate features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alamp">LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taizhou Institute of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different layers have different widths and similarity geometry. Concatenation would introduce projection assumptions. Each LAMP branch fits support-set residuals relative to CLIP, then mixes scores in common class space. If text prototypes change, the residuals must change as well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shallow texture branch and a deeper semantic branch each score cat versus dog before their scores are combined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22182-lamp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d272f3c9d6e7debd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lamp" data-paper-title="LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7084f5f48e922c1a">How does a support-bank regional kernel differ from including evaluation queries in its centering statistics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alamp">LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taizhou Institute of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both m(x) and b use the support set as the reference; queries are scored against the fixed reference. Adding test queries would make an individual result depend on the evaluation batch. Test labels must not select mixing weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With fixed support, query A uses the same calibration alone or with query B; B does not redefine the support mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22182-lamp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7084f5f48e922c1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lamp" data-paper-title="LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-35cf268cc640f6cd">Why must LAMP-F update the cached response when text prototypes change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alamp">LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taizhou Institute of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Updating prototypes changes both query priors and support residuals. The cached linear response represents how the kernel solution changes and allows exact updates without a complete solve. Updating just the query prior omits a term. Kernel statistics and mixture weights remain frozen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving the prototype toward cat images raises the prior for support cats, so their residual should shrink. Keeping the old correction double counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22182-lamp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-35cf268cc640f6cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llava" data-paper-title="Visual Instruction Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-llava-9b58a1f9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfa5b553021f92af">What does LLaVA&#x27;s visual projector do between image and answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allava">Visual Instruction Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It maps image-encoder features into visual tokens that the language model reads alongside questions and conversation history. It connects the interfaces; multimodal instruction training, not shape alone, teaches instruction following.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A width-matching projection maps encoder features to LM size, but the model still must learn which features address the user&#x27;s question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfa5b553021f92af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llava" data-paper-title="Visual Instruction Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ba55b5e7a12c6c3">Why is projecting visual features to the LLM width insufficient for following visual instructions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allava">Visual Instruction Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching shape does not align meaning. The connector learns a visual-to-language interface, and instruction supervision teaches how to answer questions conditioned on images. Projection alone does not confer recognition, localization, or multiround responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cat image can enter as a vector, but QA training is needed to answer “Where is it?”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ba55b5e7a12c6c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llava" data-paper-title="Visual Instruction Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7c311ba118b0143">How does LLaVA instruction supervision differ from CLIP&#x27;s dual-encoder contrastive training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allava">Visual Instruction Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LLaVA learns conditional answer tokens from images and questions. CLIP brings paired images and texts together in a shared embedding space for matching. Retrieval scores are not instruction-generation quality, and architecture alone does not establish superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Answering why two people hold umbrellas is conditional generation; selecting a supplied matching caption is a different output contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7c311ba118b0143">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llava" data-paper-title="Visual Instruction Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f05675cd47b434ea">Does the local two-layer projector&#x27;s negative result refute LLaVA&#x27;s instruction tuning?</h2>
