<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allava">Visual Instruction Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local run fixes a small patch encoder, classification head, and budget, and compares a linear projector with a two-layer MLP. It does not generate GPT-4 instructions or train LLaVA-13B. Extra connector capacity did not help this configuration, not all tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A decline in small clothing classification says nothing directly about large-model multiround image dialogue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f05675cd47b434ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mllmclip-2c53372a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-39e7cdcd2b99eef2">Why use a multimodal LLM teacher but keep a dual-tower MLLMCLIP student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher supplies rich cross-modal semantics but is expensive to deploy as a generator. The student distills relationships while encoding images and text independently. Teacher training cost and online retrieval cost are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distill offline, cache item image embeddings, and retrieve with a text vector without generating an answer for each item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39e7cdcd2b99eef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4e11c01b301e672">Why can CKA distill structure when teacher and student feature widths differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CKA aligns relationships between examples without coordinate-by-coordinate equality. The teacher selects informative tokens by attention; CKA constrains student image and text representations. The deployed student stays dual-tower and does not reproduce the teacher&#x27;s entire reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 1,000-dimensional teacher and 500-dimensional student can both put similar examples close without matching coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4e11c01b301e672">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-40aa0ee3239e5e79">How does attention token selection change MLLMCLIP supervision relative to distilling all tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It builds structural supervision from selected informative teacher positions across layers rather than every position. This changes information selection, not CKA&#x27;s ability to handle different widths. Selection can miss useful details, so superiority requires a controlled comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select a subset of locations when a teacher layer includes many background tokens. More tokens do not necessarily give the student more useful knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40aa0ee3239e5e79">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-55f94a382f44503d">Does the real-checkpoint path train the full CLIP student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It freezes SmolVLM2 and the CLIP encoders, trains a dimension-matching feature projection, and selects weights on separate validation. Held-out CKA and neighbor overlap do not improve consistently across three seeds. A perfect score caused by degenerate labels was invalidated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running CKA after projection checks the operator path, not full student training over the paper&#x27;s 26 benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55f94a382f44503d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-mveb-9298f9f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd709b40f21ee758">Why is MVEB&#x27;s video question answering still an embedding evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>VCQA embeds candidate answers in a retrieval pool, chooses a match for the video, and reports pool accuracy. It is not free generation. The embedding model is frozen; classification and other tasks use their prescribed probes, so output metrics differ by task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select the closest of four supplied action descriptions rather than freely generating an action and judging its wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd709b40f21ee758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4086d8bd7c3aa807">Why use identical clips for MVEB&#x27;s video-only and audio-plus-video comparison?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise changes in sample difficulty confound the contribution of audio. Keep clips paired, encoders frozen, and task-specific probes or retrieval metrics fixed; respect each model&#x27;s frame and audio configuration. An invented audio score for an unsupported model invalidates the comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate the same door-knocking video with and without sound, not a different easier clip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4086d8bd7c3aa807">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac8fad29eea9e7f7">Is forcing every MVEB video model to take 64 frames fairer than respecting its configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. MVEB uses 2 fps and up to 64 frames for variable-length models, but follows training configuration for fixed-frame models. Fixed clips are needed for audio/video pairing, and models without audio support must not receive fabricated results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Feeding 64 frames into an eight-frame model and calling the failure low embedding quality is not a fair test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac8fad29eea9e7f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-af25b7c17d30df09">Can a single cosine aggregator implement all MVEB tasks locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Official task evaluators include retrieval nDCG@10, clustering V-measure, eight-example-per-class logistic regression, and candidate QA accuracy, each with input and sampling constraints. The local page reviews resources and cost only; no model calls or formal metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieval must calculate nDCG from relevance labels. Mean cosine is neither a replacement nor QA accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af25b7c17d30df09">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:naijas2st" data-paper-title="NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-naijas2st-20646330" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e74dca2ad6800c6">What does accent diversity require in NaijaS2ST evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Anaijas2st">NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mila - Quebec AI Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pronunciation variation affects understanding and speech evaluation. Cover multiple speakers and accents, report translation directions separately, and distinguish speech-to-text from speech-to-speech. One direction or a few speakers cannot characterize all Nigerian languages or accents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>English→Hausa is not Hausa→English, and understanding one accent does not prove reliable synthesis of another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16287v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e74dca2ad6800c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:naijas2st" data-paper-title="NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbd5bc66fec4aff6">Why not use exact match against reference text for speech-to-speech translation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Anaijas2st">NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mila - Quebec AI Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Audio output needs real ASR before scoring with prescribed semantic translation metrics. Both transcription and translation errors matter. Exact text matching rejects valid paraphrases and bypasses audio. Few-shot examples come from development data, not test references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two spoken versions of “Please come tomorrow” can both be correct with different wording; preserve both the semantic and audio pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16287v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbd5bc66fec4aff6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:naijas2st" data-paper-title="NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ae01580dff4059e">Do SSA-COMET and ChrF++ measure the same kind of agreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Anaijas2st">NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mila - Quebec AI Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SSA-COMET uses a multilingual semantic model; ChrF++ mainly uses character and word n-gram overlap. The scores are complementary and not interchangeable accuracy percentages. Speech output still needs the prescribed ASR path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two valid paraphrases can preserve meaning with different character overlap; the larger number is not automatically a larger fraction correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16287v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ae01580dff4059e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:naijas2st" data-paper-title="NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4223dcd722be9bd5">What limits apply to NaijaS2ST five-shot examples and proxy language tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Anaijas2st">NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mila - Quebec AI Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Take five examples from DEV, never formal test. Some Seamless adaptations map Hausa to Arabic and Naijá to French tokens as conventions, not native model support. Local work has not downloaded audio or run complete training and evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assigning an Arabic control token for Hausa fine-tuning does not mean the audio is translated to Arabic or that untrained Hausa support exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16287v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4223dcd722be9bd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-omni-embed-mini-210068e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5145055c5225c1c3">Does Omni-Embed-Mini output new media or a retrieval vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It learns a semantic media embedding comparable to description embeddings, not image, audio, or video generation. Dense descriptions supply training targets, but the media path must still encode the input itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An audio vector comparable to a text query is representation learning; synthesizing sound from text is a generation task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5145055c5225c1c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4491baa96084cd11">Why can distilling from descriptions reduce disruption to the text backbone when adding media?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen text backbone supplies stable semantic coordinates. Dense descriptions become teacher targets; a projector and controlled LoRA learn media mappings into that space. Stop gradients through the targets, and check for relevant media information that descriptions omit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action-and-scene description anchors a video embedding, but missing small text cannot be recovered from the target alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4491baa96084cd11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a011fd986e9bb29b">What is the trade-off between frozen-text distillation and joint full-parameter multimodal training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing offers stable coordinates for new modalities and limits changes to existing text representations. Full training has broader flexibility but can shift old text capabilities. The scope of updates alone does not determine which performs better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserving existing text vectors makes an audio retrieval index easier to maintain, but text-space constraints can still limit audio-specific distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a011fd986e9bb29b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-87c149ce97e5da8a">Where should stop-gradient apply in cosine distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach the description target from the frozen text backbone. Cosine loss updates only allowed media-side parameters. The local same-space dense-description diagnostic does not train the full six-modality encoder or reproduce retrieval leaderboards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce the angle by moving the media mapping only. Updating both vectors would move the supposedly fixed semantic anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87c149ce97e5da8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-physics-mm-pretraining-bcf29586" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdcb4cabe9c03d38">Does modality synergy simply mean adding more data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It asks whether training on one modality improves knowledge or representations for another. Controlled experiments distinguish synergy from competition. Adding data alone changes compute, coverage, and task weighting together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If text reasoning improves after adding image training, check total tokens and compute before attributing it to shared knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdcb4cabe9c03d38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2bb66ec4c595c03">What do shared attention and normalization versus modality-specific FFNs control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared components allow cross-modal interactions, while separate FFNs preserve modality-specific transformations and capacity and may reduce competition. Hold data, loss weights, and budgets fixed to identify synergy; a better aggregate does not imply equal gains for every modality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Images and text use the same attention path but separate FFNs. Evaluate each separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2bb66ec4c595c03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-464a2649c054e233">How does early joint training differ from concatenating separately trained modality vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint losses update shared interaction parameters and can produce cross-modal gradient synergy or competition. Concatenation only changes downstream visible features after training; it does not create shared pretraining, even at equal data volume.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating shared attention from text and retesting vision can reveal transfer. Placing two frozen vectors side by side does not create that update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-464a2649c054e233">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1caaede64820e758">Why are joint objective weights part of the reproduction contract?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text, understanding, and generation terms have different gradients into shared parameters. The two coefficients alter their balance and therefore the conditions for synergy or competition. A runnable mini-suite or one perfect seed does not reproduce a 13.5B MoE trained on two trillion tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing generation weight tenfold changes optimization pressure although loss names stay the same.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1caaede64820e758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-retoken-1f7ac688" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-925d7e6a3ddb726f">Is ReToken&#x27;s learned RET token a fixed ID for one image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a shared learned input marker whose contextual VLM state is projected and matched to each image&#x27;s average value. Shared parameters do not imply identical query states or selected images, and the token does not encode an entire catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two questions with the same RET marker can yield different relevance scores for the same image pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-925d7e6a3ddb726f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac564f018c0c2564">Why score retrieval in the final-layer value space in ReToken?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefilled vision KV already contains image representations. Similarities in the same value space can reuse cache without rerunning an external retriever and re-encoding images. A learned retrieval token and projection adapt relevance; a frozen VLM does not eliminate supervision or guarantee generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 10 prefetched images, score their average value vectors against the new query&#x27;s retrieval token and reuse selected images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac564f018c0c2564">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3387fd902dfccf78">How does ReToken per-image BCE differ from softmax with one positive candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BCE scores each relevance label independently, weighting classes without forcing sigmoid scores to sum to one. Single-positive softmax makes candidates share probability mass. Do not silently discard valid additional positives while claiming the same supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question can require two relevant images. Both can be positive rather than relabeling one negative to force one winner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3387fd902dfccf78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cc4c368978edb1c">What is missing between ReToken&#x27;s local text cache experiment and the visual training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>WikiText-2 trains a single retrieval target, value scoring, and sparse selection, not the frozen large VLM, MIRAGE vision-language supervision, or long video. Short prefixes cannot fill top-K and affect retention. Report worse PPL as a text mechanism result, not a visual gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three history tokens and top-K ten, at most three can be retained; average retention across lengths is not a fixed compression ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cc4c368978edb1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sensenova-u1-5-44bbf8fb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccda8ef48387ba89">Do visual understanding and generation in SenseNova-U1.5 have the same input–output direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Understanding conditions on vision to answer or judge, while generation produces visual content from conditions. A unified model needs both signals. Spatial patch reconstruction concerns generation representations; expert OPD concerns post-training supervision. One operator does not establish both capabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Answering what is in an image and creating an image on request are different acceptance tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccda8ef48387ba89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48a83136d0677aa9">How does spatial patch reconstruction differ from predicting discrete image codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discrete methods use a tokenizer or VAE to turn images into codes, then predict those codes. Patch reconstruction targets local spatial structure directly and relies less on that intermediate interface. This changes representation and supervision, not proof of zero bottleneck or lower cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One method predicts codebook IDs and the other reconstructs spatial patches. Their error sources differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48a83136d0677aa9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3467848fb9faad3">How does multi-expert OPD differ from a single teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts supply different tasks or abilities; the unified model must reconcile signals rather than match one teacher distribution. Coverage can grow, but so can conflicts. More teachers do not guarantee improvement in both understanding and generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher emphasizing object relations and another emphasizing image reconstruction do not simply repeat the same target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3467848fb9faad3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-65cee03b70bff28b">Do the local masked-patch and expert OPD results establish a unified 8B model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic reference kernels and three-seed state-transition diagnostics cover masked targets and expert fusion, not multistage 8B training. Gating and loss values verify paths, not real understanding or generation benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correctly summing expert weights in a tensor does not demonstrate usable images or real visual answers from an eight-billion-parameter model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65cee03b70bff28b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-siglip2-8c923237" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27ae7a096e03b542">Does SigLIP 2 NaFlex change the number of class labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Dynamic resolution changes how vision input is represented and where compute goes. Labels are separate. SigLIP 2 combines input adaptation, global semantics, and local feature training; a fixed-resolution loss kernel does not cover the complete recipe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same cat and dog labels can accompany images of different sizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27ae7a096e03b542">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1288afe0b0bfc12f">Why add local self-distillation and masked prediction to pairwise sigmoid alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global matching constrains whole-image compatibility with text but need not train local or dense features. Local distillation and masking supervise spatial detail; captioning and data selection improve semantic inputs. Ablate these separately rather than credit sigmoid alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A street caption may only mention a car, while recovery around its masked wheel encourages finer spatial features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1288afe0b0bfc12f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-476ced67a785f2fa">How does pairwise sigmoid differ from CLIP batch softmax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Softmax normalizes over each row or column so a matching pair competes with other batch entries. Sigmoid gives each image–text pair an independent positive or negative classification term. Normalization, temperature, and bias differ; effectiveness is empirical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cat image–cat text is positive and cat image–dog text negative; sigmoid applies two separate binary constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-476ced67a785f2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15aecb074ef6effd">How do label signs and bias enter sigmoid pair loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use z=+1 or −1 in log(1+exp(−z·score)), with scaled dot product plus bias as score. Substituting 0/1 without changing the formula removes the negative gradient. Local work covers class text and masked-view consistency only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>z=−1 penalizes high negative-pair similarity; z=0 makes loss constant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15aecb074ef6effd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolvlm" data-paper-title="SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-smolvlm-5de2167d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6da8d28c15e0fd0d">Does SmolVLM just remove language-model layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolvlm">SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hugging Face</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It reallocates vision and language compute with visual token compression, tiling, positional tokens, long context, and data mixtures. Parameter count and vision input cost are separate; one rearrangement operator is not the full recipe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A smaller LM still pays vision encoding and context costs if given many high-resolution visual tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05299">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.05299-smolvlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6da8d28c15e0fd0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolvlm" data-paper-title="SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-14e67387d09772aa">Where does pixel shuffle put neighborhood information when it reduces visual token count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolvlm">SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hugging Face</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It concatenates nearby spatial tokens along channels and projects them through an MLP to the LM. It trades attention length for wider local representations rather than dropping patches. Fine text and spatial relations still require task-specific verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four adjacent patches merge into one wider vector, quartering token count but coarsening the LM&#x27;s spatial granularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05299">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.05299-smolvlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14e67387d09772aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolvlm" data-paper-title="SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ffdba7ecafa65b8">What does space-to-depth preserve compared with averaging four patches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolvlm">SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hugging Face</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Averaging erases independent patch positions; space-to-depth concatenates them in fixed spatial order so later projection can distinguish them. It trades shorter sequences for wider input tokens. Fine recognition still depends on projector capacity and training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping black upper-left and white lower-right blocks can preserve their average but change their ordered concatenation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05299">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.05299-smolvlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ffdba7ecafa65b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolvlm" data-paper-title="SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-99a7266698fe9edc">Does the local r=2 check include SmolVLM&#x27;s high-resolution and long-video recipe?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolvlm">SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hugging Face</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It uses 32×32 clothing images and 2×2 space-to-depth without high-resolution tiling, video sampling, long context, learned position tokens, or a SmolLM decoder. Results only check the rearrangement and projection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reducing 16 patches to four verifies tensor shapes, not cross-frame localization or 8,000-token context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05299">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2504.05299-smolvlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99a7266698fe9edc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-umrm-4950018b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4751b3724468f3d">Does UMRM&#x27;s unsupervised label mean no labels are used anywhere?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Caption perturbations construct preference pairs without human pairwise annotation. Layer selection uses a labeled development set, and bootstrapping uses cheap verifier labels. Preference construction, model selection, and deployment-utility supervision differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change “two cups” to “three cups” automatically, but validation labels can still determine the best layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4751b3724468f3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c4a885e90ab44ef">Why does UMRM compare all B² positive–negative pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All positives and negatives in the batch contribute ranking constraints instead of isolated pairs. Pool only response tokens so prompt/image features do not swamp response distinctions. Synthetic negatives define training signals but do not cover every real policy hallucination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positives and two negatives give four comparisons rather than two matched pairs, without creating human preference labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c4a885e90ab44ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee7e257a9c99039a">Why can caption-perturbation accuracy and real-policy selection utility move in opposite directions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic negatives may differ from actual policy errors. A reward head can learn artifacts of artificial editing. Bootstrapping on policy candidates with a verifier changes the supervision and may improve Best-of-N even if a reward benchmark falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spotting swapped colors does not ensure that a reward head can select a faithful response when policy candidates omit objects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee7e257a9c99039a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5de587fd0730601">Should UMRM change the image to match a perturbed negative description?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The external sampler edits the response while holding the image fixed. It can change a span, splice tails, shuffle clauses, or use a cross-image caption with default probability 0.15. Swapping the image changes the contrast. Do not pool image or prompt tokens into the response representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change “two dogs” to “three dogs,” but keep the original image with two dogs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5de587fd0730601">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-wemm-embedding-30d32b14" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca5d1f605b157f3e">How does interleaved WeMM input differ from a single image vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One input can combine text, images, video, and document segments in order before encoding. It represents combinations rather than indexing each modality in isolation. A shared space does not remove the need to train and validate combinations.</p>
