<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A product photo plus “same design in blue” differs from either the photo or the color term alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca5d1f605b157f3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d696f2db780b54a">Why align at scale before curated relevance and cross-scale distillation in WeMM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Initial alignment builds a shared space; refined relevance addresses items that look similar but fail the query. Distillation and Matryoshka representations carry semantics across sizes. Closeness alone is not business relevance or correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Red shoes match “red items,” but “shoes for rain” needs relevance supervision beyond appearance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d696f2db780b54a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1adb4bf127b3b1b7">How does WeMM cross-scale KD differ from supervising only the largest embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It sums teacher-to-student KL at designated Matryoshka sizes, so smaller outputs receive explicit signals. A common semantic target does not guarantee identical quality or arbitrary truncation. Compare retrieval quality and cost at specified sizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Aligning the full vector does not guarantee the first half works well; the multiscale loss explicitly supervises that distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1adb4bf127b3b1b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b68c75f5ea78fa1">Can local MovieLens Matryoshka results replace WeChat A/B?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public content and collaborative views test shared space, refinement, and truncation without the original checkpoint or private multimodal pairs. MMEB and WeChat results belong to the authors&#x27; system. Local low-dimensional proxies cannot reproduce business effects or rank on the same table.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare Recall for four- and 16-dimensional proxy vectors locally; do not project it to video-feed percentage gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b68c75f5ea78fa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some full-set questions can be answered without hearing the clip. Three text-only models identify text_cheat examples, producing the 846-example main split from 1,032 full examples. The splits answer different questions and require explicit denominators.</p>

<h2 id="qa-673875973e156d53">What do option shuffling and visual_cheat masking prevent?</h2>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shuffling reduces fixed-position bias and requires updating the private correct letter. visual_cheat masking removes videos that directly reveal the solution. Neither creates answers nor eliminates all contamination.</p>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<h2 id="qa-2a0c055e2bb4c562">Does an answer-free ActorRequest guarantee no leakage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aavmeme-exam">AVMeme Exam: A Multimodal Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for LLMs&#x27; Contextual and Cultural Knowledge and Thinking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It limits normal callback fields, but filesystem permissions, closures or question text can still leak answers. Independent process and permission audits are necessary. The fixed-A fixture tests protocol only, not capability.</p>

<h2 id="qa-f5f9c4eb25482717">Why not use Hit@1 for every MMEB-V3 task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Ammeb-v3">MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Audio, image, video and agent tasks use Hit@1; text and visual documents use NDCG@5 to retain ranking and graded relevance. Category aggregation weights tasks equally rather than pooling all queries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a task with 10,000 queries does not automatically receive 100 times the weight of one with 100 queries.</p>

<h2 id="qa-a177fb65bacfd208">Why retain the query itself and avoid target-modality prefiltering in OmniSET?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Ammeb-v3">MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The diagnostic tests both semantics and requested output modality. The query is a same-semantic, wrong-modality distractor, and twelve directions share one mixed pool. Prefiltering would hide modality-instruction failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: placing the original image first for image-to-audio retrieval has correct semantics but wrong modality and must score zero.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Ammeb-v3">MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMEB-V3 covers six categories and diagnoses modality adherence with OmniSET. MVEB focuses on video classification, clustering and eight retrieval directions with frame/audio budgets. Tasks, pools and budgets differ; neither aggregate nor local kernel substitutes for the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a capped-64-frame video experiment controls different variables from a mixed TIVA-pool diagnostic.</p>

<h2 id="qa-ef339d60e0a57a32">Why require explicit NDCG gain and exact task coverage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Ammeb-v3">MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The fixed upstream emits linear and exponential NDCG, so silently choosing one changes scores. Missing tasks also alter averages. The API enforces the gain and exact expected tasks, but cannot prove external rankings came from a real model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: omitting a difficult task invalidates a complete-category claim; a perfect fixture ranking is not model evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 复现边界与完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How do images, speech, and text connect to the same task? Does the model learn similarity or learn to generate answers?

## Takeaway

CLIP uses separate image and text encoders and a paired contrastive objective to learn shared representations for zero-shot classification and retrieval. BLIP-2 freezes the visual encoder and LLM and uses a Q-Former with a small number of queries to extract visual evidence, connecting vision and language generation in stages. Instruction tuning, distillation, reward modeling, and task-specific evaluation change supervision and readout. Track the inputs, objective, and output interface separately.

## Example

Finding the image that best matches “red umbrella” is a suitable embedding comparison. Reading the second line of small print needs fine visual evidence and a text-output interface. Connecting an image to an LLM does not automatically give it OCR, and compressed visual queries may lose details.

## Common pitfall

Retrieval similarity is not a probability of factual correctness. Matching words does not prove the image was used. Check negative controls such as shuffled images and distinguish natural image–text pairs, speech accents, and video domains. Small-image runs, random fixtures, and public benchmarks support different claims.

## Reading order

Start with CLIP's dual encoders, normalization, and contrastive loss. Then read BLIP-2's Q-Former and two-stage connection to distinguish shared embeddings from language generation. Choose later work on instruction tuning, distillation, rewards, or evaluation to match your task.

1. [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)
2. [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597)

## Check your understanding

Can a high CLIP retrieval score establish that the model reads all text in an image?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Contrastive pairing mainly constrains overall image–text compatibility. Small text needs enough visual resolution, local representations, and decoding supervision. Evaluate OCR or the relevant fine-grained task separately and verify that results change with image content.

</details>
